Text: This is actually a much bigger deal for Bittensor than it may seem at first.

A lot of subnet builders hold most of their capital in alpha. But teams still need liquid TAO to pay developers, cover infrastructure, and keep growing.

Until now, that usually meant selling alpha.

@MentatLend_ introduces another option: deposit your alpha as collateral, borrow TAO against it, and keep the alpha staked and earning emissions while you use the borrowed TAO to fund operations.

In simple terms, builders can access liquidity without immediately selling the position they worked to build.

There’s another side to it too.

TAO holders can deposit their TAO into a lending pool and earn yield from borrowers. Even the unused TAO in the pool remains productive through root staking, so the goal is to offer lenders a return above ordinary root staking.

There’s another side to it too.

TAO holders can deposit their TAO into a lending pool and earn yield from borrowers. Even the unused TAO in the pool remains productive through root staking, so the goal is to offer lenders a return above ordinary root staking.

The first market is already live with @webuildscore on SN44:

→ Deposit TAO and earn additional yield
→ Deposit SN44 alpha as collateral
→ Borrow TAO without selling that alpha
→ Keep the collateral staked and earning emissions
But what I find most interesting is what happens when more subnet markets are added.
Each subnet can eventually develop its own borrowing rate based on demand and risk. That gives the ecosystem a completely new signal.
Alpha price tells us where people see upside.

Borrowing rates can tell us where the market sees risk.

Bittensor already has markets for intelligence and ownership. Mentat Lend is now adding something the network has never really had before: a native credit market.

That could change how teams fund themselves, how TAO moves through the ecosystem, and how subnet risk is understood. 

Definitely worth paying attention to this one.
